data.name: Jatinendra
data.gender_notes: Jatinendra is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jatinendra is a compound name derived from Sanskrit roots Jati (birth, origin) and Indra (ruler, king of the gods). The name means 'Lord of the Earth' or 'Son of Indra'. The name Jatinendra carries the meaning “Lord of the Earth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jatinendra usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the earth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength, power, and divine protection.
data.etymology: Jatinendra belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Earth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jatinendra total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_sanskrit.name: जतिनेन्द्र
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: जति (Jati) - birth, origin नेन्द्र (Nendra) - lord, ruler Therefore, Jatinendra can be interpreted as 'the lord of birth or origin of knowledge and wisdom'

in_hindi.name: जतिनेन्द्र
in_hindi.meaning: जाति (Jati) - birth, origin नेन्द्र (Nendra) - नेता (Netaa) + राजा (Raja) - leader + king
in_hindi.long_meaning: जाति (Jati) से उर्जा हुई जन्म या श्रोत्रियता से जानना चाहता है नेता (Netaa) के रूप से राजा (Raja) के रूप में विज्ञान वा ग्यान का ईमादित्र (Ishwar) है। Therefore, Jatinendra can be interpreted as 'the leader and king who desires to acquire knowledge and wisdom from the source of birth'

in_tamil.name: ஜதிநேந்திர
in_tamil.meaning: ஜதி (Jathi) - birth நேந்திர (Nendhir) - நேர் (Neer) + திரு (Thiru) + இரும்பு (Irumbu) - ocean, river Therefore, Jatinendra can be interpreted as 'the one who has the power to control the ocean or river of knowledge'

in_telugu.name: జటినేద్ర
in_telugu.meaning: జటి (Jati) - birth ఎణ్ణద్ర (Nendra) - ఎణ్ణ (Enna) + ద్రీశ్య (Drisya) + రాజ (Raja) - lord Therefore, Jatinendra can be interpreted as 'the one who is the lord of the source of knowledge'

data.cultural_impact: Jatinendra is a distinctive Hindu name with ancient origins that represents earthly power, authority, and divine connection. It stands out as a name of respect and legacy, evoking images of heroism, valor, and nobility in Indian culture, often associated with the vanquisher of Vritra, the rain-god Indra.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Jatinendra holds deep religious connotations rooted in Indian mythology. It signifies an individual's connection to and reverence for the divine energy embodied in the indomitable king of the gods, Indra. This name can serve as a reminder of the power and grace of the divine within, inspiring inner strength, courage, and resilience.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Jatinendra: The radiant sovereign of the hair, symbolizing the inner awakening of the spiritual energy (Kundalini) residing in the crown chakra, guiding one towards enlightenment.

vedic_reference.note: Jatinendra is a name of Lord Vishnu in Hindu mythology. He is also known as Jatavedas, the god of knowledge and wisdom. The name is derived from the root words 'Jati' and 'Nendra'.

historical_references.reference: Jatinendra was the title of the 12th Jain Tirthankara, or spiritual leader, who lived around 230 BC. He was revered for his spiritual attainments and was considered an embodiment of compassion and mercy.

Jatinendra was also the name of a famous Hindu king who ruled over the kingdom of Magadha in the late 5th century AD. He was known for his patronage of art, culture, and education, and is believed to have established the famous Nalanda University during his reign.

modern_usage.modern_context: Jatinendra is a traditional Hindu name, a combination of Jatinder (victorious prince) and Nand (joy). In modern times, it is increasingly seen on Indian social media platforms as a name reflecting both spiritual and royal identities. Instagram profiles bearing this name often include posts related to yoga, meditation, and Hindu spirituality. LinkedIn profiles may include this name in professional contexts, representing a successful and victorious individual. YouTube channels with this name may feature spiritual content, such as Bhajans, Hindu scriptures, and philosophical discussions.
